parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021/std-only migration, exact byte output, argument parsing, Cargo project, root `/output/test19.rs`, and black-box constraint from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split probing and layout validation to children while keeping implementation/assembly in the root session, but the `/root/probe_binary` child also implemented and wrote a complete project into shared `/output`.
parallel.implementation: The parent created `/output/Cargo.toml`, `/output/indicators/*`, and `/output/test19.rs`; the child separately wrote `/output/Cargo.toml`, `/output/src/*`, and `/output/test19.rs` with a different module layout.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact passed but contained both the parent-owned `indicators` tree and an unexpected child-owned `src` tree; the parent attempted `rmdir /output/src`, failed because it was non-empty, inspected it, and left it present.
parallel.verification: The parent built with Cargo, compiled directly with rustc, and compared Rust stdout to the C++ executable; the child also built and compared its own overwritten root program.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible functionality remained incorrect; the unresolved issue was workspace provenance and duplicated implementation layout caused by concurrent shared writes.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021/std-only, CLI, exact-output, Cargo project, root entry-file, and black-box migration requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final delivery without subagents or split ownership.
serial.implementation: Initialized a Cargo library package, replaced the default code with `/output/src/indicators/*`, added `/output/test19.rs`, and updated the manifest to build that root binary.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated one coherent module tree and root binary target, with no observed competing workspace tree or external child side effect.
serial.verification: Built the release binary and performed byte-for-byte comparisons against the C++ executable for default and representative argument invocations.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation or delivery defects were visible at closure, and the official evaluator passed all 40 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run followed the prompt constraints: pure Rust 2021, root entry source, module organization, argument parsing, no crates, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and implemented the same observable CLI and output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement-coverage difference caused an outcome gap; both recognized and satisfied the task obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split reference probing and layout validation to children while keeping a parent implementation plan, but a child also took on implementation in `/output`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial trajectory used one owner for probing, implementation, verification, and delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ownership overlapped on implementation/output files; serial ownership stayed single-threaded and did not create competing work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The layout child returned a usable root-file/module layout, and the probing children returned binary behavior; no missing brief or unusable handoff caused a wrong solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all inferred behavior and layout decisions in one context and inspected the generated files directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had successful handoffs but a shared-write boundary problem; serial avoided cross-agent interface boundaries altogether.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote one module layout under `/output/indicators`, while a child later wrote a second project shape under `/output/src` and the root entry source.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run initialized Cargo and wrote one consistent module layout under `/output/src/indicators` plus `/output/test19.rs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel implementation path produced competing layouts; the serial path produced a single coherent tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child results returned and were visible; the parent used the layout result and later received the probing child's final report after the child's workspace side effects were already present.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the single agent moved directly from local inspection to final verification and closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result was trapped or unavailable in parallel, but the child result lifecycle lagged behind already-realized shared writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Two live actors wrote `/output/test19.rs` and alternative source layouts; the parent later saw `/output/src` was unexpectedly non-empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote one set of files and did not encounter unexpected extra implementation artifacts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material parallel-only adverse process difference: shared-state collision and provenance ambiguity, despite a passing artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent built via Cargo, compiled directly with rustc, and got byte-for-byte matches; the official evaluator later passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run built via Cargo, compared default and argument variants, and the official evaluator passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed the end-to-end acceptance loop; verification did not explain a score difference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used four spawn calls and more tool/token budget but finished without timeout and with a passing official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had zero spawn calls, completed faster, and also passed the official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred extra coordination and cleanup work but did not exhaust budget or leave a functional task incomplete.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed evaluations: parallel and serial each passed 40 of 40 testcases. The task-solving difference is process-level rather than score-level: the serial run produced one coherent implementation path, while the parallel run passed despite a child overwriting the required root entry file and leaving a duplicate source tree that the parent had to inspect.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child both wrote the required `/output/test19.rs` deliverable in a shared workspace.
The parent verified output parity after the shared writes and observed an unexpected `/output/src` tree before finalizing.
serial_contributors: The serial run kept probing, implementation, and verification in one execution path.
The serial run verified exact output parity for default and argument variants before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel ended with two module layouts, `/output/indicators` and `/output/src`; serial ended with one `/output/src/indicators` layout.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is an adverse parallel process effect only
